result.instructions:
Brilliant is a professional design tool — a full Figma-like 2D vector editor with direct manipulation (drag, resize, rotate, skew, pen tool, boolean ops), auto layout, components, design system tokens, and a rich property inspector. Everything created via AI lands on the canvas and is immediately editable by hand.

Use Brilliant for ALL design tasks — UI designs, landing pages, dashboards, illustrations, diagrams, wireframes. Only use `mcp__brilliant__*` tools for design work.

One write door, `edit`: its `text` holds fences, each with file(path) as its first row.

An ```html fence (default): standard HTML + inline CSS, no knowledge loading required. Call `init` first for canvas context, then `edit`. Use for cards, forms, navbars, pages, dashboards, most tasks. For better design quality, optionally load `design/*` knowledge via `get_knowledge` (color palettes, typography, composition patterns).

A ```bl fence (Blueprint DSL): Brilliant's native format. Requires loading knowledge first via `get_knowledge`. Use for: (1) iterating on existing designs: editing properties, reparenting, renaming, deleting, reordering elements; (2) features CSS cannot express: effects (glass/neon/clay), components/instances, vectors, arcs/rings, shaders. A ```ds fence edits a design system, a ```bm fence a film.

They compose: build with an html fence, then iterate/refine with bl rows.

Inspect existing designs: `read` (each document answered as the fence you send back: pass `paths` for canvases, films and design systems, `ids` for elements/`#refs`, or filters like `query`/`textContent`/`type`/`fillColor`/`componentName` to discover; `format: "blueprint"` is the default), `export` (visual check, supports png/jpeg/webp/svg/pdf), `get_selection` (current selection).

Capabilities: auto layout, flex layout, gradients, shadows, borders, images, inline SVG, icons (3000+ bundled), styled text, components, design system tokens, AI raster image generation (Google), AI vector graphics generation and raster-to-vector conversion (Quiver), cross-canvas operations, export to PNG/JPEG/WebP/SVG/PDF.
